historical_reviews.deepseek: Its likely section label is useful only after the PDB is mapped; the six-line slice can omit board/serial/custom fields or select a generic power record and does not define correctness.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly gates the passive query on expected data and Web confirmation. The current review separates immutable FRU identity from live PDB/rail telemetry and handles multiple distribution assemblies.

original_test_intent: Validate the identity record for every applicable power-distribution board: prove the correct PDB FRU is present and readable, its required manufacturing/service fields match the installed assembly, and BMC Web presents the same information.
original_method: Map the chassis power-distribution topology to FRU device identities, capture the entire read-only inventory, decode each PDB record, compare its fields with the approved board/BOM source and have an operator verify the corresponding Web object while retaining power-health context.
manual_activity: The power/platform owner enumerates installed PDB assemblies, binds each to its FRU/Web object and approved BOM data, confirms any optional fields and judges mismatches. Automation performs only the protected inventory comparison.
required_inputs: Chassis/SUT identity and installed PDB count, location, PN and revision
Power topology including PDB-to-PSU/rail domain solely for identity correlation
BMC/FRU firmware and stable per-PDB FRU device/area identifiers
Rules for blank, duplicated, placeholder, encoding and revision values
BMC Web object and field mapping for each installed PDB
Supported read-only ipmitool path and credential handling
Power/BMC baseline, evidence retention and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Do not infer the PDB from the first Power Distribution text match
Collect and retain every FRU record before extracting the mapped PDB object
Do not confuse live voltage/current/PMBus data with FRU identity acceptance
Never issue FRU edit, PMBus write, rail enable, power-cycle, reset or firmware action
Do not clear SEL or OS logs by default; preserve the baseline
Use secret-safe access and redact credentials without deleting diagnostic fields
Stop on missing/duplicate FRU IDs, unexpected board count, malformed data, rail/BMC anomaly or inventory instability
agent_execution_scope: Confirm exact row and installed PDB applicability
Fingerprint the power topology without changing it
Collect complete FRU list/print data and resolve mapped PDB device areas
Compare all required identity/service fields with the approved matrix
Prepare each matching BMC-Web object for operator review
Record unchanged power/BMC/SEL/OS health before and after
Do not test rails, write FRU or set a verdict
engineer_actions: Approve installed PDB and FRU device mapping
Provide BOM/field truth and optional-field rules
Confirm Web mapping and resolve stale/duplicate identities
Assess serviceability impact and issue the result

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The underlying `fru print` is an appropriate passive source, but `grep -iA6 Power Distribution` destroys record boundaries and may return a generic or partial object. It omits multi-PDB completeness, Web parity and the field oracle, and passes the password on the command line.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Through approved secret-safe BMC access, archive the complete FRU inventory, select each PDB by its owner-approved device/area and physical mapping, compare the full required field matrix, then correlate the mapped Web objects.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: PDB, FRU list, readable/correct/Web criteria and 10/10-minute estimates remain unchanged; no PDB count, section name or expected value is guessed.

modernized_recommendation.status: REQUIRES PER-PDB FRU AND BOM MAPPING
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Enumerate physical PDB assemblies, map them to stable FRU records, compare complete identity/service fields against the BOM, verify all Web representations and retain a read-only power-health snapshot to demonstrate collection caused no disturbance.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the generic PDB label deterministic across chassis variants and separates identity evidence from live power behavior.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A readable Power Distribution snippet cannot prove the installed PDB PN/revision/serial or all required boards; PMBus telemetry cannot replace FRU identity.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Querying is low risk, but wrong FRU-to-board association can cause incorrect field replacement, service inventory or root-cause conclusions during a power incident.

project_override_considerations: A platform with an integrated or non-field-replaceable PDB must document which parent FRU owns the PDB fields or mark the row not applicable with engineering approval. It must not fabricate a separate FRU or reuse an I2C/PMBus result.
expected_evidence: Source variant, chassis and BMC/FRU version identity
Installed PDB location/PN/revision and power-domain map
Per-PDB FRU device/area and BMC-Web object mapping
Complete redacted raw FRU inventory and command status
Decoded per-PDB field comparison including missing/duplicate/placeholder results
Timestamped Web parity evidence and unchanged power/rail/BMC/SEL/OS baseline/post state
No-write/no-clear audit, recovery notes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The Master row consistently requests a PDB FRU read and Web comparison. Its generic name and absent expected values require project mapping but do not contradict its own procedure or criteria.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Once the installed PDB and field matrix are supplied, complete read-only FRU/Web comparison is a deterministic operation. These are readiness inputs rather than an irreducible ambiguity.

review_improvement: Establishes per-PDB physical-to-FRU provenance, prevents power telemetry from being mistaken for identity proof and turns a partial text filter into complete BOM/Web reconciliation.
independent_technical_reasoning: A power-distribution board may be integrated, duplicated or represented under a chassis-specific FRU name. Matching the words Power Distribution cannot establish which board or service identity was returned. The meaningful check begins with the actual PDB population and maps each board to a complete FRU record; live rail data is retained only to show the management query did not disturb power. With that package, automation can compare data while the engineer owns correctness and applicability.
